_hinweis: Demo feed cards, one for each perspective in the overview (same order). Reworded from the comments in fallstudien/01_metallbau_heidekamp.md: one specific problem, clear to all teams, plus one line of context. Nothing added. Images and memes: original AI-generated images (public/karten), no well-known meme templates; the joke is about situations, never people or teams.

f1.text: Customer changes reach Engineering only as voice messages.
f1.kontext: Customers request changes over the phone, and these are passed on in the evening.

f1.text: No one knows for sure which drawing version is on display in Workshop.
f1.kontext: Drawings are often changed several times.

f1.text: Updated drawings do not reach Workshop in time.
f1.kontext: Result: a railing was built using the old version.

f1.text: On site, the dimensions do not match the fabricated parts.
f1.kontext: Result: parts have to be shortened and welded again on site.

f2.text: Parts that were planned for the job are missing on site.
f2.kontext: Result: a trip back, and half the morning is gone.

f2.text: Materials taken from stock are not recorded anywhere.
f2.kontext: Result: people have to search for materials.

f2.text: Office finds out too late that materials are running out.

f3.text: Office does not know when Installation is at the customer's site.
f3.kontext: Customers ask for updates, and Office has to call around.

f3.text: Calls asking about job progress keep coming in on site.
f3.kontext: Result: work is interrupted again and again.

f4.text: The practical knowledge in Workshop is not written down anywhere.
f4.kontext: New staff ask experienced staff at every step.

f5.text: Posts are welded by hand, one at a time, often for a whole day.
f5.kontext: The same movement over and over.

f6.text: Stair stringers and railing sections are carried by hand to upper floors.
f6.kontext: Often up to the third floor.

memes.text: Me when the system says: “12 still in stock.”
The phone on the scaffolding, for the fourth time: “Are you there yet?”
